clue.text: Scheme to get extremely large pastries from the Orient

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the east means reading from right to left, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: mega is slang for extremely large
tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: A plot to obtain enormous cakes imported from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the Orient' turns MEGATARTS round: in an across entry the east is the right-hand end.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a cunning plan or ruse is a scheme.

clue.text: Maybe farmer's a source of litter on farm? I'm not sure

parts.words: a source of litter on farm
parts.note: a sow is a female pig, which gives birth to a litter of piglets
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: A hesitant guess about whether a farmer is to blame for rubbish on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish but means a brood of piglets. The definition is by example, flagged by 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer is one example of someone who scatters seed in a field.

clue.text: Dire game across Atlantic, involving ball

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: involving means the round letter is taken into the middle of the phrase

parts.note: seen from Britain, across the Atlantic is in the US
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A grim report on some sport played in America involving a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across Atlantic' is read from Britain: over the ocean means in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something disastrous or catastrophic is dire.

clue.text: Before river, draw level

indicators.note: the draw is put before the river, reversing the order the clue mentions them

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch something flat in front of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one layer or level in a stacked arrangement, such as seating.

clue.text: Fed European but not head of state

indicators.note: but not means the following letters are left out of the word

parts.note: a German is a European
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: Someone fed by a European, though not a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like a verb, but it is the US slang noun for a federal agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are American slang for an FBI agent, a federal law officer.

clue.text: Bright individual flower maiden's kept in memory

indicators.note: kept in means these letters are held within the word for memory

parts.note: mind can mean memory, as in bring to mind
an aster is a daisy-like flower
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A clever person remembers the flower a young woman kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius or very clever person is a bright individual.

clue.text: What includes Post Office counter's opening time

indicators.note: includes means the interjection holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: eh? is said in place of what?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Asking what time the post office counter opens.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period or era, a span of time.

clue.text: Many quite outraged and one's kept calm

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters keep the extra letter within them
outraged suggests the words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Plenty of people were quite incensed while one person stayed composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outraged' rearranges MANY QUITE, and 'kept' holds I inside that anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Equanimity is composure, a noun matching 'calm' used as a noun.

clue.text: Person knocking on door's let out after dropping round

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order
after dropping means one letter is first removed from the words

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A visitor knocking at the door is let in after making a delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after dropping' takes one O out of DOORSLET, leaving DORSLET, which 'out' rearranges. 'Knocking on' is an idiom for getting old, not rapping at a door.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone knocking on in years is elderly, an old person.

clue.text: Workers not working comfortably

parts.note: hands are manual workers
a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Staff off duty, taking it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To win by a wide margin is to win easily, without effort.

clue.text: Poet's refrain about English imperialist notion

indicators.note: about means the poet's name goes around the letter

parts.note: Walt Whitman was an American poet
a burden is the refrain or chorus of a song

explanation.surface: A poet's recurring line concerning England.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem gave the phrase its name; here Whitman, not Kipling, is the poet in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's phrase for the supposed duty of colonisers to rule other peoples, an imperialist idea.

clue.text: Castle of Otranto's walls besieged by kings

indicators.note: besieged by means surrounded by the royal letters

parts.note: R (rex) and K are both abbreviations for king

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: The fortifications of The Castle of Otranto, the Gothic novel, under siege by monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the rook is also called the castle.

clue.text: Try to defend Blair over core principles

indicators.note: over means the whole construction is turned backwards
to defend means to guard by surrounding

parts.note: to seek is to try, as in seek to do
Tony Blair was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: An attempt to stand up for Tony Blair about his central beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole container round, so the result reads backwards from how it was built.
explanation.definitionFit: A keynote is a central theme or principle, so the plural fits core principles.

clue.text: Uncertain German admitted to not having sex

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the other word

parts.note: continent means sexually abstinent

explanation.surface: A German confesses, unsure, to celibacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continent' here means self-restrained, not a landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: Contingent means dependent on chance, so not certain.

clue.text: Overdid a little drink — date is going badly

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: going badly suggests the letters are going wrong, into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone drank slightly too much while a date went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going badly' rearranges DATE IS into ATISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise is to exaggerate or make a fuss, which is overdoing it.

clue.text: Affectionate message retiring chap's received is really grand

indicators.note: received means the chap's name takes in the other letters
retiring means drawing back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Mark is a man's name, a chap
so means really, as in so good
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A loving note a shy man received is truly wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses MARK to KRAM, and 'received' takes ISSOG inside it. A kissogram is a delivered greeting with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting delivered by someone who kisses the recipient, a message of affection.

clue.text: Snatched a little butter, then had rest

parts.note: a kid is a young goat, which butts
napped means had a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed a small pat of butter before a sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is one who butts: a little one is a kid, a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to seize someone, so the past tense means snatched.

clue.text: Traveller wants nothing sweet after a brandy

indicators.note: after puts the nothing and the sweet behind the brandy

parts.note: marc is a brandy made from grape skins
O looks like zero, nothing
Polo is a British brand of mint sweet

explanation.surface: A traveller turning down a dessert after a glass of brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant famous for journeying to China, a celebrated traveller.

clue.text: Where potter may be skilful, pocketing ball in the end

indicators.note: pocketing means the word holds the letter inside it, as a snooker pocket holds a ball

parts.note: deft means skilful

indicators.note: in the end points at the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A snooker player skilfully sinking a ball at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' looks like a snooker player but is someone making pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft, in the Netherlands, is famous for its blue and white pottery.

clue.text: Face of Lancôme provided with swell launch

indicators.note: the face of a word is its first letter

parts.note: if means provided that
a swell is a fashionable toff

explanation.surface: A cosmetics brand's face cream given a smart launch.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a rocket leaves the ground is its launch.

clue.text: Little old lady close to Russian revolutionary

parts.note: minute means tiny
ma is one's mother, colloquially the old lady

indicators.note: close means the end, so this takes the final letter

explanation.surface: A small elderly woman near a Russian radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutemen were American militia in the War of Independence, ready to fight at a minute's notice.

clue.text: Island arrived at by air, perhaps

parts.note: to make a place is to arrive at it

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word could be in another form, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: An island reached by flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portuguese island in the Atlantic, famous for its fortified wine.

clue.text: Females in a cool, periodically wintry, feeling of kinship

indicators.note: in means the women go inside the next words

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
F stands for female, so two of them are FF

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Women in a chilly, sometimes wintry setting feeling close.
explanation.definitionFit: An affinity is a natural liking or sense of connection with another.

clue.text: Divine figure from sculptor needing no introduction

indicators.note: no introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor

explanation.surface: A statue of a god by a famous sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: New setter's joining Times, a selfish sort?

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'm
by means times, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A new crossword setter joins The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A nimby (not in my back yard) objects to local development, hence the query.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposing nearby building only because it affects them may be called selfish.

clue.text: See 15
Run one?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
an ace is a one on a playing card or die

explanation.surface: A question whether to organise a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: to run one would be to hold a contest of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Running one is staging a contest of speed, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: High standards for Lisa Simpson, working with energy

indicators.note: working means set in motion, the letters reworked

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Lisa Simpson, the cartoon swot, working hard to excel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges FOR LISA SIMPSON plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionalism is the competence and conduct expected of a skilled worker, high standards.

clue.text: Make lean daughter grilled feta

indicators.note: grilled feta is cooked, changed, so its letters move

explanation.surface: A daughter is told to slim down with grilled cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove fat from meat is to make it lean.

clue.text: One may be travelling dry road around Middle East

definitions.text: One may be travelling dry road around Middle East

indicators.note: around means the anagram goes around the region's letters
travelling suggests the letters move about

explanation.surface: A camel trekking along a desert road across the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges DRY ROAD and 'around' puts it round ME. The whole clue also describes the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-humped camel, a desert animal used for transport across arid lands.
